posts.title: Website checklist for dental clinics
posts.hook: A patient with a cracked tooth at 11pm is reading your website, not calling you.
items: Treatments with price ranges
A range for a cleaning or a filling helps someone comparing clinics decide to call you.
Dentists' names and training
Show the actual dentists, where they trained, and a photo taken in your own clinic.
Insurance and emergency hours
List which insurers you work with and when you can see someone who is in pain.
Tap-to-call and a map pin
On a phone, your number should dial with one tap and your address should open a map.

posts.title: Website checklist for restaurants
posts.hook: Someone is standing outside deciding whether you're open. Your site should answer first.
items: Hours and phone at the top
Put tonight's hours and your number in the header, before the photo of the dining room.
The menu as a page, not a PDF
Dishes as text on the page can be read on a phone and updated when the fish changes.
Your own reservation line
Tell people how you take bookings: phone, WhatsApp or a link, in your own words.
Your name on a page you own
Keep your name, address and menu on your own page, so a search leads to you.

posts.title: Website checklist for law firms
posts.hook: Nobody searches for 'law firm.' They search for a problem. Your site should start there.
items: One page per practice area
Give family, employment or immigration work its own page on how a matter usually starts.
Attorney bios, credentials first
Bar admissions, years in practice and languages spoken first. Hobbies much later.
Experience without case promises
Describe the kinds of matters you handle. Leave out outcomes, since every case differs.
A clear way to ask for a consultation
Say how a first consultation works, what it costs if anything, and how to request one.

posts.title: Website checklist for real estate agents
posts.hook: Your brokerage page looks like every other agent's. Buyers remember a face and a street.
items: Your photo and your story up top
Open with who you are, where you work and how long you've sold homes there.
An offer to value their home
Sellers start by wondering what their place is worth. Tell them how to ask you.
Neighborhood guides, one per area
Write what you tell buyers in the car: schools, commute, the good bakery, noisy roads.
A link to your current listings
Point to where your active listings live so buyers see them next to your name.

posts.title: Website checklist for accountants
posts.hook: 'Contact us for pricing' on a basic tax return. You could just put a starting price.
items: Service tiers with starting prices
Bookkeeping, payroll, year-end accounts, each with a 'from' price so people self-select.
The software you work in
Name the bookkeeping software you support so a prospect knows their files will open.
Three questions before the call
Ask business type, size and what they need up front, so the first call is about them.
Who you are and your registrations
State your qualifications and registrations in the footer, where people look for them.

posts.title: Website checklist for personal trainers
posts.hook: Clients come from Instagram referrals. Then they ask where to sign up. There's no answer.
items: Online and in-person, priced apart
Remote coaching and sessions at the gym cost different amounts. Give each its own block.
Client photos with permission
Show real progress from real clients, with their consent and only what they want shared.
How to start, in one place
Say what happens first: a call, a form, a trial session. Put it where new clients land.
Your packs, written plainly
Four sessions, twelve sessions, a monthly plan. One line each on who it suits.

posts.title: Website checklist for florists
posts.hook: Orders come by DM, which works until you lock up at 6. A website keeps answering at night.
items: This week's bouquets, with prices
Show what's in the shop this week, a price next to each, so people can decide at home.
Subscriptions explained simply
Weekly or monthly flowers, what size, how to start. Three lines beat a phone call.
Same-day cutoff, stated plainly
Say 'order by 1pm for same-day delivery' and name the neighborhoods you deliver to.
A 'pick me something' WhatsApp link
Some people want you to choose. Give them one tap to say budget, occasion and address.

posts.title: Website checklist for pizzerias
posts.hook: It's 7pm, a family of five is hungry, and your number is at the bottom of a PDF menu.
items: Your number, tap to call, top right
On a phone, the number should dial with one tap, and sit before the dough photos.
Reservations in your own words
Tell people how you take tables: phone, WhatsApp, walk-in only. Keep it on your page.
The menu as text on the page
Pizzas as a list people can read on a phone, and change when the burrata runs out.
A gallery that loads quickly
Six good photos of the oven and the pizzas beat forty that take ten seconds to appear.

posts.title: Website checklist for coaches
posts.hook: Prospects find you on LinkedIn, read three posts, then look for how to hire you. Nothing.
items: Packages with honest prices
A six-session package and a monthly retainer, each priced, so people know your level.
A clear way to book a first call
Say how a first conversation happens and how long it takes. Make the link easy to spot.
Your approach before your CV
Explain how you actually work with someone before you list the certifications.
Testimonials with a name and city
'Maria, Lisbon' is believable. 'Client, Europe' is wallpaper. Ask first, use real names.

posts.title: Website checklist for wedding photographers
posts.hook: Instagram books your weddings. It can't tell a couple whether they can afford you.
items: A starting price, visible
'Weddings from' with a number saves you and the couple a week of polite emails.
Eight weddings, chosen carefully
Pick the weddings that look like the ones you want more of. Archive the rest.
Your style in one sentence, at the top
Candid and documentary, or posed and editorial? Say it before they scroll.
Dates you still have open
List the months you're still taking for next season so couples know whether to ask.

posts.title: Website checklist for yoga studios
posts.hook: A new student wants to know what's on tomorrow at 7am. Your website should know too.
items: The schedule on the homepage
This week's classes, times and teachers on the first page, readable on a phone.
Drop-in prices stated plainly
A single class, a five-pack, a monthly pass. Prices next to each, no 'inquire within'.
Teacher bios written by humans
Where they trained, what they teach, and one line about why. Skip the stock quotes.
A clear first-class offer
Make the first visit easy to understand: what to bring, where to park, what it costs.

posts.title: Website checklist for gyms
posts.hook: The intro offer is why people join, and it sits three scrolls down under a stock barbell.
items: Intro offer at the very top
A trial week or first class goes first, with how to claim it, before the gallery.
Class schedule on your own page
Keep this week's timetable on your site, so people find it without leaving.
Trainer bios that name names
Each coach: photo, specialty, classes they teach. Their followers come along too.
Membership tiers side by side
Off-peak, full access, classes only. One column each, with what's included and price.

posts.title: Website checklist for consultancies
posts.hook: You do bespoke strategy work. Your website could belong to any freelancer with a laptop.
items: Engagements with a shape and a price
A two-week audit, a quarterly retainer. Name the deliverable and a starting price.
Case studies that load fast
Problem, what you did, what changed, in a few paragraphs. One image, no 40MB deck.
A direct way to book a conversation
Say who the first call is for and how to get one, so the wrong leads filter themselves.
No fake logo wall
Name clients you can actually name. Three real ones beat twelve you have to blur.

posts.title: Website checklist for event planners
posts.hook: The best work you've done is in Instagram stories that expired. Couples can't see it now.
items: A portfolio on your own site
Pick ten events, name the venue and the season, and keep them on a page that stays up.
Starting prices per package
Full planning, month-of coordination, day-of only. Each with a price it starts from.
Your style, stated before credentials
Rustic, minimal or maximalist: say which one you do best before listing your training.
An inquiry form that asks the basics
Date, guest count, venue if booked, budget range. Four fields save three emails.

posts.title: Website checklist for online tutors
posts.hook: Parents compare tutors at 10pm once the kids are asleep. They want a rate, not an email.
items: A section per subject and level
Exam prep, high school math and university entrance each get their own section.
Hourly rate and lesson packs
One hour, five lessons, ten lessons. State each price so parents can plan the term.
A free intro lesson, explained
Say how long it is, what you cover, and how to request it.
Book directly with you
Tell parents how to schedule with you, so they don't go back to a marketplace.

posts.title: Website checklist for marketing agencies
posts.hook: 'We help brands grow.' So does every agency in town. Your homepage has one line to differ.
items: Services with a scope and a price
Paid search setup, a monthly content retainer. What's included, and what it starts at.
Case studies as short cards
Client, problem, what you did, in a card that opens to the full story.
A team page that earns its place
Real names, real photos, what each person owns. Skip the headshot of the office dog.
An intake with three questions
Budget range, timeline, what's broken. Ask before the call, so the call is useful.

posts.title: Website checklist for designers
posts.hook: Your portfolio sits on a platform beside everyone else's. Clients can't see where you end.
items: Type that stays out of the way
Choose one typeface and let the work carry the color. Your site is the frame.
Eight projects, not eighty
Pick the work you want more of. Each gets a short note on the brief and your role.
Availability and a rate band
'Taking projects from March, day rate from' and a number filters the wrong inquiries.
Your email, written out
Put your address in plain text so a prospect can paste it into an email to their boss.

posts.title: Website checklist for independent bookstores
posts.hook: Staff picks on Instagram, events on a chalkboard. Someone searching tonight sees neither.
items: Staff picks with a voice
A paragraph from the person who read it, with their name. Keep the last twelve up.
Events on your own page
Readings, book clubs and signings with date, time and how to reserve a seat.
Newsletter signup near the top
One field and one sentence on what people get: new arrivals, events, staff picks.
Easy to read from the shop floor
Someone standing in your aisle might check it. Big text, phone number and hours first.

posts.title: Website checklist for ceramic artists
posts.hook: You sell in small drops. A generic shop template expects a warehouse.
items: A page for the current drop
Show what's available now, say when the next drop opens, and leave sold pieces visible.
Your story before the pots
Where the studio is, what clay you use, how long a piece takes. Then the products.
No marketplace in the middle
Sell from your own page so the customer remembers your name and comes back to you.
A product grid that works on a phone
Two pieces per row, large photos, price visible, so it reads on a phone screen.

posts.title: Hair salons: Instagram portfolio
posts.hook: Instagram is your portfolio, and Google has never seen it.
posts.fix_title: Twelve cuts on a page you own
posts.fix_body: Put twelve Instagram cuts on a gallery page, your salon's name and street next to them.

posts.title: Hair salons: stylists uncredited
posts.hook: Each stylist has a following. Your website doesn't mention one name.
posts.fix_body: Photo, specialties and how to book with them by name. Their followers land on your site.

posts.title: Dental clinics: outdated site
posts.hook: The clinic site hasn't changed since 2009. The equipment has.
posts.fix_body: Show the rooms as they are now, the team as it is now, and take down the old banner.

posts.title: Dental clinics: insurance questions
posts.hook: You've answered 'do you take my insurance?' a hundred times by phone.
posts.fix_title: An insurance section, with a list
posts.fix_body: Name the insurers you work with and what to bring. Add 'ask us' for anything else.

posts.title: Dental clinics: appointments by phone only
posts.hook: The only way to get an appointment is to call while you're drilling.
posts.fix_title: Say how to request a visit
posts.fix_body: WhatsApp, a short form or a callback request, with your reply hours. All beat voicemail.

posts.title: Restaurants: PDF menu and stock photo
posts.hook: Your website is a 2021 PDF menu and a stock photo of a salad.
posts.fix_body: Your phone, tonight's special, your light. It beats a studio shot of a stranger's food.

posts.title: Restaurants: hidden hours
posts.hook: To find your hours, diners scroll through other people's reviews.
posts.fix_body: Today's hours, last orders, and the day you're closed. All of it above the photos.

posts.title: Restaurants: third-party reservations
posts.hook: People book your tables on a site that isn't yours and keeps the credit.
posts.fix_title: A page that carries your name
posts.fix_body: Name, address, menu and how to book on your own page. Link out only if you must.

posts.title: Law firms: outdated site
posts.hook: Your firm's site is from 2012. The partner who 'owns' it lost the login.
posts.fix_title: A site anyone at the firm can edit
posts.fix_body: When a new associate joins or an address changes, someone should fix it the same day.

posts.title: Law firms: thin practice pages
posts.hook: One bullet list covers every practice area. That's where people search.
posts.fix_title: A full page per practice area
posts.fix_body: What the matter involves, how you work, what to bring to the first meeting. No promises.

posts.title: Law firms: vague intake
posts.hook: Intake is a contact form that says 'we'll be in touch.' When, exactly?
posts.fix_title: Say what happens after they write
posts.fix_body: Who reads it, how fast they'll hear back, and what the first consultation covers.

posts.title: Real estate agents: templated brokerage page
posts.hook: Your brokerage page is the same one every other agent at the office got.
posts.fix_title: A page that is only yours
posts.fix_body: Your photo, the neighborhoods you actually work, and how to reach you directly.

posts.title: Real estate agents: invisible on portals
posts.hook: Buyers find the listing on a portal and never learn who's selling it.
posts.fix_title: Your face next to every listing
posts.fix_body: On your own page, each listing sits beside your name and your phone number.

posts.title: Real estate agents: no time for neighborhood guides
posts.hook: Buyers love neighborhood guides. You never have an evening to write one.
posts.fix_body: Write the one you sell most, in the words you use in the car. Add another next month.

posts.title: Accountants: contact for pricing
posts.hook: The pricing page says 'call for a quote.' For a monthly payroll run.
posts.fix_body: Monthly bookkeeping, annual returns, payroll. A 'from' price lets the right people call.

posts.title: Accountants: long intake calls
posts.hook: Half of every intake call is finding out what the prospect needs.
posts.fix_body: Business type, revenue range, what they need help with. The call starts where it should.

posts.title: Accountants: software unstated
posts.hook: You live in one bookkeeping system. Your site just says 'accounting.'
posts.fix_title: Name the software you work in
posts.fix_body: A plain sentence on which systems you support, so prospects know their files will open.

posts.title: Personal trainers: nowhere to book
posts.hook: Clients come from Instagram, then DM you asking how to actually start.
posts.fix_title: One page that says how to start
posts.fix_body: A free consult, a trial session, a form. Pick one and link it from your Instagram bio.

posts.title: Personal trainers: one price for two services
posts.hook: Online and in-person cost different amounts. Your site shows one price.
posts.fix_body: Remote plan on the left, gym sessions on the right, what's included under each.

posts.title: Personal trainers: programs hidden in an app
posts.hook: The programs live in a coaching app that nobody finds from a search.
posts.fix_title: Describe the programs on your site
posts.fix_body: Name each program, who it's for, how long it runs, how to get it. The app comes after.

posts.title: Florists: DMs as order book
posts.hook: Instagram DMs are your order book. They stop at closing time.
posts.fix_title: An order path that works at midnight
posts.fix_body: List what's in stock, delivery areas and a way to order or message. The site stays open.

posts.title: Florists: delivery area questions
posts.hook: Customers message you just to ask whether you deliver to their street.
posts.fix_body: Name the neighborhoods and the cutoff time for each. Add a note for anywhere else.

posts.title: Florists: subscriptions by phone
posts.hook: You make lovely subscription boxes. The only way to sign up is to call.
posts.fix_body: Weekly or monthly, two sizes, a price each, and how to start. Three lines do it.

posts.title: Pizzerias: booking provider owns your name
posts.hook: Search your pizzeria's name and the booking provider comes up first.
posts.fix_title: Your own page for your own name
posts.fix_body: Name, address, hours, menu, how to book, on a page you own. The provider gets a link.

posts.title: Pizzerias: phone number buried
posts.hook: Your number is on the napkins and the box. Not at the top of your site.
posts.fix_body: One phone number, top of every page, that dials when tapped on a phone.

posts.title: Pizzerias: PDF menu
posts.hook: The menu is a PDF from 2019. One price change means a call to a friend.
posts.fix_title: A menu you can edit yourself
posts.fix_body: Pizzas as text on the page, grouped by type, prices you can change on a Tuesday night.

posts.title: Coaches: nowhere to book
posts.hook: They read your posts for a month, look for where to book, and give up.
posts.fix_title: A booking path in your bio and site
posts.fix_body: Link to one page that explains the first call and how to get one. Same link everywhere.

posts.title: Coaches: discovery calls
posts.hook: Discovery calls eat your week. Nothing on the site filters who gets one.
posts.fix_title: Say who you're for and who you're not
posts.fix_body: 'I work with first-time managers in tech' saves ten calls with people you can't help.

posts.title: Coaches: site looks cheap
posts.hook: You charge a premium rate. Your site looks like a weekend side hustle.
posts.fix_title: Look like the price you charge
posts.fix_body: Fewer words, bigger type, one photo of you, packages with prices. Remove the clip art.

posts.title: Wedding photographers: unqualified inquiries
posts.hook: Couples DM you for a package at a third of your price, every week.
posts.fix_body: 'Weddings start from' and a number, before the gallery. The right couples keep reading.

posts.title: Wedding photographers: template sites
posts.hook: Photographer sites share one template. Couples can't tell who shot what.
posts.fix_body: Open with one sentence on how you shoot and one photo only you would have taken.

posts.title: Wedding photographers: buried inquiry form
posts.hook: The inquiry form is four clicks deep, so couples DM you on Instagram.
posts.fix_body: Date, venue, guest count, how they found you. Four fields, one button, every screen.

posts.title: Yoga studios: template sites
posts.hook: Every studio site has the same sunset, the same lotus, the same font.
posts.fix_body: Your floor, your light, your teachers mid-class. Nobody else has those.

posts.title: Yoga studios: schedule off-site
posts.hook: The class schedule sits on a booking provider's page. Searches miss it.
posts.fix_title: Schedule on your own site too
posts.fix_body: List this week's classes on your page in plain text, and link to booking from there.

posts.title: Yoga studios: slow updates
posts.hook: A teacher moves her Tuesday class. The site shows it wrong for a month.
posts.fix_body: Class times and teacher bios should take minutes to change, no HTML friend required.

posts.title: Gyms: signup through software page
posts.hook: Your membership signup page carries the software's name, not your gym's.
posts.fix_body: Explain memberships, prices and the intro offer on your own site. Then link to signup.

posts.title: Gyms: invisible trainers
posts.hook: The trainers have followers. The website has a stock kettlebell photo.
posts.fix_title: A trainer grid with real names
posts.fix_body: Photo, specialty, classes they teach. Their followers find your gym through them.

posts.title: Gyms: buried intro offer
posts.hook: The intro offer that brings people in is three scrolls down.
posts.fix_title: Intro offer on the first screen
posts.fix_body: What it is, what it costs, how to claim it. Above the gallery, above the mission.

posts.title: Consultancies: no packages
posts.hook: Your work is bespoke. Your site has no packages, no prices and no shape.
posts.fix_body: A two-week assessment, a quarterly retainer. Name the output and a starting price.

posts.title: Consultancies: budget on calls
posts.hook: Half of each discovery call is spent finding out the budget.
posts.fix_body: 'Engagements start at' with a number saves both sides a 45-minute call.

posts.title: Consultancies: case study updates
posts.hook: Updating one case study takes a designer and three rounds of feedback.
posts.fix_body: Problem, approach, outcome in text you can edit yourself, with one image. One evening.

posts.title: Event planners: portfolio on Instagram
posts.hook: Your portfolio is on Instagram. Search engines can't read your stories.
posts.fix_title: Ten events on your own site
posts.fix_body: Venue, season, guest count and three photos each. A page that's still there next year.

posts.title: Event planners: how much for a wedding
posts.hook: Every inquiry opens with 'how much for a wedding?' The site never says.
posts.fix_body: Planning from, coordination from, day-of from. Three numbers answer the first email.

posts.title: Event planners: style invisible
posts.hook: Rustic, minimal or maximalist? Couples can't tell until they meet you.
posts.fix_title: Your style, named at the top
posts.fix_body: One sentence and three photos that prove it, before any mention of years in business.

posts.title: Online tutors: marketplace cut
posts.hook: The marketplace takes a cut, and the parent never learns your last name.
posts.fix_title: A direct way to book you
posts.fix_body: Your own page with your rate, your subjects and how to schedule. Send parents there.

posts.title: Online tutors: rate by email
posts.hook: Parents have to email you to learn your hourly rate.
posts.fix_body: Hourly, five-lesson and ten-lesson prices, for each subject if they differ.

posts.title: Online tutors: subjects lumped together
posts.hook: Exam prep, calculus, competition math. Your site says 'tutoring.'
posts.fix_body: What you cover, which level, which exam, and a line on how you teach it.

posts.title: Marketing agencies: generic positioning
posts.hook: 'We help brands grow.' Twelve agencies within a mile say the same thing.
posts.fix_body: 'Paid search for dental clinics in Ohio' is a position. 'Growth partner' is a shrug.

posts.title: Marketing agencies: unqualified leads
posts.hook: Half your discovery calls are with companies that can't afford you.
posts.fix_body: 'Retainers start at' and a number. Add the three questions you always ask first.

posts.title: Marketing agencies: case studies off-site
posts.hook: Your case studies live in a slide deck nobody can find from your site.
posts.fix_title: Case study cards on the homepage
posts.fix_body: Client, challenge, what you did, one image. Link the full deck from each card.

posts.title: Designers: platform profile
posts.hook: A platform profile isn't a site you can send a client to close the deal.
posts.fix_title: A site with your name on the URL
posts.fix_body: Selected work, a short bio, a rate band, a plain email. Nothing else competing.

posts.title: Designers: template tell
posts.hook: Clients spot a template portfolio. From a designer, they expect more.
posts.fix_body: One typeface, generous white space, your work at full width. The site shouldn't compete.

posts.title: Designers: weekend redesigns
posts.hook: You spent another weekend redesigning your portfolio instead of billing.
posts.fix_title: Ship it, then do client work
posts.fix_body: Eight projects, one paragraph each, publish. Revisit in six months, not six days.

posts.title: Independent bookstores: staff picks on Instagram
posts.hook: Staff picks go on Instagram, where a search engine can't read them.
posts.fix_body: The book, the staff member's name, and two sentences on why. Add one every week.

posts.title: Independent bookstores: events by word of mouth
posts.hook: The events calendar is a chalkboard by the till. Nobody online sees it.
posts.fix_body: Date, time, author, how to reserve a seat. Future events first, past ones below.

posts.title: Independent bookstores: stock questions
posts.hook: Customers call to ask if a book is in stock. You're already on a call.
posts.fix_title: Say how to check and reserve
posts.fix_body: A phone line, WhatsApp or an email for 'do you have it?' and the hours you answer.

posts.title: Ceramic artists: marketplace cut
posts.hook: The marketplace takes a cut of every mug and shows buyers your rivals.
posts.fix_body: Your pieces, your prices, your story, and a buyer who remembers your name next time.

posts.title: Ceramic artists: generic store
posts.hook: On that platform, your store looks like every other handmade store.
posts.fix_body: Open with your wheel, your kiln and your hands in clay. Products come second.

posts.title: Ceramic artists: drops vs catalog
posts.hook: You release twelve pieces a month. The template wants a thousand SKUs.
posts.fix_title: Show the drop, date the next one
posts.fix_body: Current pieces, sold ones marked sold, and 'next drop opens' with a date at the top.

posts.show: Service menu with prices, stylist profiles, WhatsApp button.

posts.title: Example prompt: Flower shop in Nişantaşı, Istanbul

posts.show: Weekly bouquets, subscriptions, delivery areas, WhatsApp.

posts.different: Wood-fired oven built by the owner's uncle from Naples.

posts.title: Example prompt: Leadership coach in Amsterdam

posts.title: Example prompt: Wedding photographer in Bodrum, Turkey
posts.different: Shoots outdoor weddings on the coast, never a posed group shot.
posts.show: Selected weddings, pricing from, style note, inquiry form.

posts.title: Example prompt: Yoga studio in Trastevere, Rome
posts.different: Classes in Italian and English, small groups of eight.
posts.show: Schedule, drop-in prices, teachers, first class offer.

posts.title: Example prompt: Small strength gym in Portland, Oregon
posts.who: Small strength gym in Portland, Oregon.
posts.different: Barbells, kettlebells and coaching, with no cardio machines in sight.
posts.show: Intro offer, class schedule, trainers, membership tiers.

posts.title: Example prompt: Supply chain consultancy in Rotterdam
posts.different: Two former port logistics managers who now advise importers.
posts.show: Engagements with prices, case studies, team, book a call.

posts.title: Example prompt: Event planner in Barcelona
posts.different: Specializes in small weddings of under sixty guests in old farmhouses.
posts.show: Portfolio, packages from, style, inquiry form.

posts.title: Example prompt: Online math tutor based in Toronto
posts.who: Online math tutor based in Toronto.
posts.different: Teaches high school calculus and exam prep over video, evenings only.
posts.show: Subjects, hourly rates, free intro lesson, how to book.

posts.title: Example prompt: Marketing agency in Manchester
posts.different: Paid search only, for independent dental and vet clinics.
posts.show: Services with prices, case studies, team, intake questions.

posts.title: Example prompt: Freelance brand designer in Copenhagen
posts.different: Logos and packaging for food brands, nothing else.
posts.show: Selected work, about, availability and rates, email.

posts.title: Example prompt: Independent bookstore in Kızılay, Ankara
posts.different: Half the shelves are poetry, the rest are the owner's picks.
posts.show: Staff picks, events, newsletter signup, hours and map.

posts.title: Example prompt: Ceramics studio in Porto
posts.different: Monthly drops of twelve pieces, glazed with local seaweed ash.
posts.show: Current drop, next drop date, studio story, contact.

posts.title: Small business website tip: the first screen
posts.hook: The first screen has to answer three things before anyone scrolls.
posts.tip_title: What, where, and what to do next
posts.tip_body: Say what you do, which town you do it in, and give one button. Everything else can wait.

posts.title: Small business website tip: phone numbers on mobile
posts.hook: The phone number is on the site, in an image, where no thumb can tap it.
posts.tip_title: Make the number a real link
posts.tip_body: Type it as text and link it, so on a phone one tap dials. Test it on your own phone.

posts.title: Small business website tip: opening hours
posts.hook: Someone in your parking lot is checking your site before getting out.
posts.tip_title: Hours, today first
posts.tip_body: Show today's hours at the top, and name the holidays you close. Keep it current.

posts.title: Small business website tip: address and map
posts.hook: 'Near the station' is not an address.
posts.tip_title: Full address, plus a map link
posts.tip_body: Street, number, floor if any, and a link that opens directions. Mention parking.

posts.title: Small business website tip: real photos
posts.hook: A stock photo of a smiling stranger says nothing about your shop.
posts.tip_title: Your people, your place
posts.tip_body: Phone photos of your actual team and room, in daylight. Replace them every year.

posts.title: Small business website tip: page speed
posts.hook: Your homepage carries a 20MB video of clouds. Your customer is on a bus.
posts.tip_title: Make it load on a weak signal
posts.tip_body: Resize photos before uploading, drop the autoplay video, test it on mobile data.

posts.title: Small business website tip: plain headlines
posts.hook: 'Solutions for a changing world' fits a bank, bakery or a funeral home.
posts.tip_title: Headline says what you do
posts.tip_body: 'Bike repair in Ghent, same day' beats any slogan. A stranger should get it in a glance.

posts.title: Small business website tip: one clear next step
posts.hook: Call, email, book, download, subscribe, follow. Six buttons, no action.
posts.tip_title: One button per page
posts.tip_body: Decide the single thing you want a visitor to do, and make that the only large button.

posts.title: Small business website tip: prices
posts.hook: 'Contact us for a quote' makes the visitor do work you could have done.
posts.tip_title: Publish a starting price
posts.tip_body: A 'from' price or a typical range gives people a yardstick before they write to you.

posts.title: Small business website tip: reviews
posts.hook: A review from 'Happy Customer' convinces no one.
posts.tip_title: Reviews with a name, by permission
posts.tip_body: Ask if you can quote them with their first name and town. Keep their exact words.

posts.title: Small business website tip: contact options
posts.hook: Some people will never call. Others will never fill in a form.
posts.tip_title: Offer two ways to reach you
posts.tip_body: A number to call and a way to write, email or WhatsApp, on every page. Say reply times.

posts.title: Small business website tip: footer basics
posts.hook: The footer gets no love and all the trust questions.
posts.tip_title: Footer: address, hours, legal name
posts.tip_body: Full address, phone, hours, legal business name, privacy page. Boring and essential.

posts.title: Small business website tip: menus
posts.hook: Home, About, Services, Solutions, Resources. For a two-person shop.
posts.tip_title: Four menu items, plain words
posts.tip_body: Name pages after what people want: Prices, Hours, Gallery, Contact. Cut the rest.

posts.title: Small business website tip: readable text
posts.hook: Light gray text at 13 pixels on a white background is a dare.
posts.tip_title: Big, dark text on a plain ground
posts.tip_body: Body text at 18 pixels or more, strong contrast, short paragraphs. Check it in sunlight.

posts.title: Small business website tip: alt text
posts.hook: A beautiful gallery, completely invisible to a screen reader.
posts.tip_title: Describe every photo in alt text
posts.tip_body: Describe what's in it: 'bakery counter at 7am, bread cooling.' Search engines read it.

posts.title: Small business website tip: keeping information current
posts.hook: The homepage still wishes everyone a happy 2023.
posts.tip_title: Set a monthly ten-minute check
posts.tip_body: Hours, prices, team, the news section. Fix or delete anything that has gone stale.

posts.title: Small business website tip: the owner's story
posts.hook: Your 'About' page is a mission statement with no human in it.
posts.tip_title: Four sentences from the owner
posts.tip_body: Who you are, why you started, where you learned it, what you still enjoy. Add a photo.

posts.title: Small business website tip: FAQs
posts.hook: You answer the same six questions by phone every single day.
posts.tip_title: Put the six questions on the site
posts.tip_body: Write them exactly as customers ask, with short honest answers. Add more as they come.

posts.title: Small business website tip: domain name
posts.hook: The business lives at a free subdomain with a string of numbers in it.
posts.tip_title: Your own name, your own domain
posts.tip_body: Match the name on your sign. Short, spellable over the phone, no hyphens.

posts.title: Small business website tip: what happens after contact
posts.hook: Someone fills in your form. Then: silence. For how long?
posts.tip_title: Say what happens next
posts.tip_body: 'We reply within one working day, usually from Anna.' Set the expectation, then meet it.

posts.title: Website copy rewrite: Plumber in Leeds
posts.before: Quality plumbing services for all your needs.
posts.after: Burst pipe in Leeds? We come out the same day, evenings included.
posts.why: It names the problem, the place and a promise you can actually keep.

posts.title: Website copy rewrite: Bakery in Lyon
posts.before: Fresh baked goods made with passion.
posts.after: Sourdough and croissants, baked at 5am in Croix-Rousse.
posts.why: Specific bread, a specific hour and a specific district. Passion is assumed.

posts.title: Website copy rewrite: Dog groomer in Denver
posts.before: We love your pets like our own!
posts.after: Dog grooming in Capitol Hill. Nervous dogs welcome, one dog at a time.
posts.why: The second line tells an anxious owner exactly why they should pick you.

posts.title: Website copy rewrite: Yoga studio in Munich
posts.before: Find your inner balance with us.
posts.after: Morning yoga in Schwabing, 7am and 8:15am, in English and German.
posts.why: Times, place and language answer the questions a new student has before 'balance.'

posts.title: Website copy rewrite: Accountant in Dublin
posts.after: Bookkeeping and year-end accounts for Dublin tradespeople and shops.
posts.why: Saying who you serve lets the right people recognize themselves in one line.

posts.title: Website copy rewrite: Florist in Ankara
posts.after: Fresh bouquets in Çankaya, same-day delivery if you order by 2pm.
posts.why: An occasion is vague; a neighborhood and a cutoff time are something to act on.

posts.title: Website copy rewrite: Dentist in Toronto
posts.before: Comprehensive dental care in a comfortable setting.
posts.after: Family dentist in Leslieville, evening slots Tuesday and Thursday.
posts.why: A working parent gets a reason to click, and the line makes no claims about care.

posts.title: Website copy rewrite: Pizzeria in Naples
posts.before: Authentic Italian cuisine for the whole family.
posts.after: Wood-fired pizza in Vomero, open till midnight, takeout at the window.
posts.why: 'Authentic' is on every pizzeria's site. A closing time is a fact worth knowing.

posts.title: Website copy rewrite: Wedding photographer in Porto
posts.after: Documentary wedding photos in Porto and the Douro, no posed lineups.
posts.why: It says how you shoot and where, so couples who want that style know they've found it.

posts.title: Website copy rewrite: Personal trainer in Austin
posts.before: Transform your body and your life.
posts.after: Strength coaching in East Austin for beginners over forty, 6am starts.
posts.why: Who it's for and when it happens matter more than a promise about someone's life.

posts.title: Website copy rewrite: Bookstore in Edinburgh
posts.before: A wide selection of books for every reader.
posts.after: Secondhand fiction and poetry on Leith Walk, open late on Thursdays.
posts.why: A specialty and a late night give someone a reason to walk in. 'Wide selection' doesn't.

posts.title: Website copy rewrite: Hair salon in Istanbul
posts.after: Curly hair specialists in Cihangir, walk-ins welcome before noon.
posts.why: Two nouns and a neighborhood do what a slogan can't: tell someone it's for them.

posts.title: Website copy rewrite: Electrician in Glasgow
posts.before: Professional electrical services you can trust.
posts.after: Rewires and fuse boards in the West End of Glasgow, evening callouts.
posts.why: Naming the jobs and the area lets a worried homeowner match you to their problem.

posts.title: Website copy rewrite: Math tutor in Vancouver
posts.before: Helping students reach their full potential.
posts.after: Grade 11 and 12 math online, weekday evenings, first lesson free.
posts.why: Potential is abstract. A grade, a time slot and a free first lesson are concrete.

posts.title: Website copy rewrite: Cafe in Krakow
posts.before: Great coffee, great atmosphere, great people.
posts.after: Filter coffee and cardamom buns in Kazimierz, open from 7am weekdays.
posts.why: Three greats say nothing. One bun and an opening time say exactly what to expect.
